correctness.rationale: For gamma=0 the series diverges; for 0<gamma<=0.63 compare with a geometric series of sum 1/(3^gamma-1)>1. On [0.63,0.99], 14 rational intervals use monotonic lower bounds of the first 300 positive terms and 65-digit directed-decimal enclosures, minimum margin >0.0011064. For gamma in [0.99,1], compare gamma-dependent products with q0=49/25 beta products; the exact beta-integral telescoping identity yields B_j bounds. The derivative splits into the first five negative terms (certified upper < -1.47), positive terms 6..1000 (upper < 0.81), and a rigorous integral tail (upper <0.08). Hence phi prime<-0.58, and since phi(1)=1 it is >1 to the left. Full proof specifies uniform convergence and all boundary cases. CHECKER.py was executed from its actual packaged path and independently spot-checked with a second interval method; finite output supports exactly the enclosures used by the proof, not an unproved infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: A recent mathematically motivated model imposes the exact nontrivial strict series bound as its key hypothesis for a coupling-based convergence result and explicitly leaves its full validity unsettled. The new global proof closes that precise hypothesis for every strict sublinear exponent, with a tiny 14-cell rational certificate and analytic tail control. It distinguishes the sharp gamma=1 equality boundary, and avoids claiming independent graph convergence or any two-community conjecture. Computational assistance does not by itself create value; the resolution of a specific stated parameter gap does.
